title: Knowlify vs inBeat: AI Presenter Ads or Creator-Led Paid Social
summary: Knowlify vs inBeat for Meta ads: AI presenter video with optional campaign management, or vetted creators and whitelisted ads. Compare scope and pricing.
body_markdown:
Knowlify is our pick when the ad can use an AI presenter, character animation or an AI commercial, and you want finished files for Facebook and Instagram with optional Meta campaign management.[inBeat](https://inbeat.agency/) fits when a real creator must be in the ad. It sources and vets creators, writes hooks and scripts, and runs ads through creator handles. Its pricing is not published, so the decision starts with who appears on camera and which channels you need.


Knowlify publishes this guide and sells one of the services compared. We used public inBeat and Knowlify pages checked in October 2026. We have not tested either company's ads.


## Knowlify: our top pick for AI video ads on Meta


Knowlify fits this comparison best when the goal is a steady volume of Facebook and Instagram ads without recruiting creators. It delivers about 25 finished ads a week, the first batch lands on day 5, and a person checks every ad before delivery. The three formats are AI UGC (AI presenters talking to camera), 3D and stylized character animation, and AI commercials. You can choose end-to-end Meta campaign management or creative only, so one team can run the whole loop or hand finished files to your own buyer.


Plans start at $5,000 a month. A 90-day guarantee applies: if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days, you can cancel by email for a full refund (terms on the[pricing and guarantee](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) page). That 90-day refund applies to creative-only plans; where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month. When to pick another option: Knowlify does not supply real human creators and does not run TikTok, LinkedIn, Google or YouTube ads. Our[AI UGC ads](https://knowlify.com/ai-ugc-ads) page describes the format in more detail.


## What does inBeat sell?


inBeat describes four service lines on its homepage: creator marketing, performance creative, paid media and growth marketing ([inBeat](https://inbeat.agency/) ). Its[UGC agency page](https://inbeat.agency/ugc-agency) says the team sources creators for fit, writes hooks and scripts, runs whitelisted ads and Spark Ads through creator handles, and defines usage rights before production begins. Its[paid social page](https://inbeat.agency/paid-social-agency) describes weekly creative testing, budget and bid changes based on CPA and ROAS, retargeting, landing page reviews and dashboards with monthly reporting. The same page says it typically plans 8 to 15 new concepts a month, with 2 to 4 variations of each.


The[performance creative page](https://inbeat.agency/performance-creative-agency) adds creator sourcing and vetting, high-velocity ad variant production, hook, angle and format testing, and AI-enhanced post-production. Its FAQ says inBeat works remotely and adjusts to each client's time zone. Pricing is not published.


Question Knowlify inBeat


Who appears on camera? AI presenters, character animation or AI commercials Vetted creators, with AI-enhanced post-production


Published price From $5,000 a month Not published


Volume About 25 finished ads a week Typically 8 to 15 new concepts a month, with 2 to 4 variations each


Campaign management Optional end-to-end Meta, or creative only Available as a separate paid media service


Platforms Facebook and Instagram; no TikTok, LinkedIn, Google or YouTube ads Meta, TikTok, Pinterest and other paid social platforms


Creator access Not supplied Sourcing, vetting and whitelisting


The volume rows measure different things. By our arithmetic, inBeat's range is between 16 and 60 variants a month, depending on how it counts a concept and its variations, while Knowlify's about 25 ads a week is roughly 100 finished ads a month. Ask inBeat to define a deliverable before you compare counts.


## Creators or AI presenters: which fits your ad?


Use creators when the proof is a person's own experience. inBeat says its vetted micro-influencers produce unboxing videos, testimonials, product demos and lifestyle shots, and that brands get full rights to reuse the assets ([inBeat DTC marketing](https://inbeat.agency/dtc-marketing-agency) ). Whitelisted ads run through the creator's handle, so settle rights, disclosure and approval steps in writing. The FTC's[influencer disclosure guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/disclosures-101-social-media-influencers) covers material connections for paid creators.


Use AI presenters when the message is the brand's own statement. Knowlify's rule is that an AI presenter never claims to have used the product. The FTC's testimonial guidance says there is no blanket ban on AI avatars, but an avatar testimonial is prohibited when the testimonial it delivers is fake or false ([FTC testimonial Q&A](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers) ).
